title: The Semantics of Propositional Logic
subtopics: Inductive definition of truth value τ̂(φ)

definitions.definition: A function τ: A → {0,1} that assigns a truth value to every propositional variable.
A formula φ is satisfiable if there exists a truth assignment τ such that τ̂(φ) = 1.
A formula φ is valid (a tautology) if τ̂(φ) = 1 for every truth assignment τ.
Two formulae φ and ψ are equivalent (φ ≡ ψ) if they have the same truth value in every truth assignment.
φ is a semantical consequence of φ₁, …, φₙ (written φ₁, …, φₙ ⊨ φ) if every truth assignment that satisfies all premises also satisfies φ.

algorithms: Inductive evaluation of truth value τ̂(φ)
Truth-table method for checking validity and satisfiability
examples: p → q, p ⊨ q (modus ponens is semantically valid)
learning_objectives: Define and compute truth assignments and truth values.
Determine whether a formula is satisfiable, valid, or unsatisfiable.
Verify semantical consequence using truth tables.
